newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Grain - Buyers remain bearish on corn.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain - Buyers remain bearish on corn.

text.p: East Asian buyers expect corn prices to continue to ease on near ideal growing weather in U.S. crop areas, but said the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) stocks report, due later on Monday, would have limited impact.
"We expect the USDA report for corn to be a little bearish and corn prices to fall further," a trader with a major South Korean feed milling company said.

The bearish outlook for corn is expected to bring the Korea Corn Processing Industry Association (KOCOPIA) and another buying group into the market for three shipments totalling 150,000 tonnes for October arrival, traders said.
Other Korean buyers were choosing to stay out of the market on projections of further price declines, they added.
Traders said Korean flour milling companies were also likely to stay away from the wheat market after brisk purchases for August/September shipments in the past few weeks.
In Japan, buyers said they would buy U.S. corn this week for the fourth quarter, partly encouraged by lower freight rates across the Pacific Ocean.
Corn premiums are currently at about 95 U.S. cents a bushel over CBOT September futures, traders said.
"We'll cover U.S. corn for fourth quarter supplies this week. Unlike soybeans, we're not worried about supplies of U.S. corn this year, and will keep buying at the usual pace," one trader said.
In Taiwan, traders said the USDA stocks and acreage report would have a minor impact on Chicago corn futures.
"We are focused more on weather conditions for corn now," a buyer said. "People will disregard the USDA corn report unless there are major changes."
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan were quoted at about $11.00 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized June shipments.
Taiwanese wheat buyers are expected to stay sidelined this week as most of the island's nearby demand has been met by recent purchases.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association on Friday bought two 33,000-tonne wheat shipments at tender for July and August deliveries, traders said.
